verses.1:1: The word of the Lord that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.
verses.1:2: The beginning of the word of the Lord in Hosea. And the Lord said to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a wife of prostitution and children of prostitution, because the land will surely commit prostitution away from following the Lord."
verses.1:3: And he went and took Gomer, daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
verses.1:4: And the Lord said to him, "Call his name Jezreel, because in a little while I will avenge the blood of Jezreel on the house of Judah, and I will put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel;
verses.1:5: and it will be in that day that I will shatter the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel."
verses.1:6: And she conceived again and bore a daughter. And He said to him, "Call her name 'Not Shown Mercy,' because I will no longer continue to show mercy to the house of Israel, but rather I will surely oppose them.
verses.1:7: But I will show mercy to the sons and will save them by the Lord their God, and I will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by war, nor by horses, nor by horsemen."
verses.1:8: And she weaned Not Shown Mercy, and she conceived again and bore a son.
verses.1:9: And He said, "Call his name 'Not My People,' because you are not My people, and I am not yours."
verses.2:1: And the number of the sons of Israel was like the sand of the sea, which will not be measured out nor counted; and it will be in the place where it was said to them, "You are not My people," they also will be called sons of the living God.
verses.2:2: And the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel will be gathered together, and they will establish for themselves one rule, and they will go up out of the land, because great is the day of Jezreel.
verses.2:3: Say to your brother, "My People," and to your sister, "Shown Mercy."
verses.2:4: "Contend with your mother, contend, because she is not My wife, and I am not her husband. And I will remove her prostitution from My presence and her adultery from between her breasts,
verses.2:5: so that I may strip her naked and restore her just as on the day of her birth; and I will make her a wilderness and set her like a waterless land, and I will kill her with thirst;
verses.2:6: and I will certainly not show mercy to her children, because they are children of prostitution.
verses.2:7: For their mother committed prostitution, she who bore them acted shamefully, because she said, 'I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water and my garments and my linens, my oil and all that is due to me.'
verses.2:8: Therefore, look, I am hedging up her way with thorns, and I will wall up the ways, and she will certainly not find her path;
verses.2:9: and she will pursue her lovers and will certainly not overtake them, and she will seek them and will certainly not find them. And she will say, 'I will go and return to my former husband, because it was better for me then than now.'
verses.2:10: And she did not know that I gave her the grain and the wine and the oil, and I multiplied silver for her; yet she made things of silver and gold for Baal.
verses.2:11: Therefore, I will return and take back My grain in its season and My wine in its appointed time, and I will take away My garments and My linens so as not to cover her indecency;
verses.2:12: and now I will uncover her uncleanness in the sight of her lovers, and no one will by any means rescue her out of My hand;
verses.2:13: and I will turn away all her joys, her festivals and her new moons and her Sabbaths and all her festive assemblies;
verses.2:14: and I will lay waste her vine and her fig trees, of which she said, 'These are my wages that my lovers gave me,' and I will make them a testimony, and the wild beasts of the field and the birds of the sky and the creeping things of the earth will devour them;
verses.2:15: and I will punish her for the days of the Baals in which she offered sacrifices to them, and put on her earrings and her necklaces, and went after her lovers, but she forgot Me," says the Lord.
verses.2:16: "Therefore, look, I am leading her astray and will set her like a wilderness, and I will speak to her heart,
verses.2:17: and I will give her possessions to her from there, and the valley of Achor to open up her understanding; and she will be humbled there according to the days of her infancy and according to the days of her going up out of the land of Egypt.
verses.2:18: And it will be in that day," says the Lord, "that she will call Me 'My Husband,' and she will no longer call Me 'Baals';
verses.2:19: and I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and their names will certainly no longer be remembered.
verses.2:20: And I will make a covenant for them in that day with the wild beasts of the field and with the birds of the sky and the creeping things of the earth; and I will shatter bow and sword and war from the earth, and I will cause you to dwell in hope.
verses.2:21: And I will betroth you to Myself forever; and I will betroth you to Myself in righteousness and in justice and in mercy and in compassions,
verses.2:22: and I will betroth you to Myself in faithfulness, and you will come to know the Lord.
verses.2:23: And it will be in that day," says the Lord, "that I will listen to the sky, and it will listen to the earth,
verses.2:24: and the earth will listen to the grain and the wine and the oil, and they will listen to Jezreel.
verses.2:25: And I will sow her for Myself on the earth, and I will love Not Loved, and I will say to Not My People, 'You are My people,' and he will say, 'You are the Lord my God.'"
verses.3:1: And the Lord said to me, "Go again and love a woman who loves evil things and is an adulteress, just as God loves the sons of Israel, yet they look to foreign gods and love cakes with raisins."
verses.3:2: And I hired her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer of barley and a jar of wine,
verses.3:3: and I said to her, "For many days you will remain for me, and you will certainly not commit prostitution nor belong to a man, and I will be for you."
verses.3:4: Because for many days the sons of Israel will remain with no king, nor ruler, nor sacrifice, nor altar, nor priesthood, nor manifestations.
verses.3:5: And after these things the sons of Israel will return and seek the Lord their God and David their king, and they will be amazed at the Lord and at His good things in the last days.
verses.4:1: Hear the word of the Lord, sons of Israel, for the Lord has a judgment against those who dwell in the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God upon the land.
verses.4:2: Cursing and falsehood and murder and theft and adultery have been poured out upon the land, and they mingle blood upon blood.
verses.4:3: Therefore the land will mourn, and it will be diminished together with all who dwell in it, with the wild beasts of the field, and with the creeping things of the land, and with the birds of the sky, and the fish of the sea will vanish,
verses.4:4: so that no one may plead a case, nor may anyone rebuke. But My people are like a priest spoken against,
verses.4:5: and he will grow weak by day, and a prophet will grow weak with you; I have likened your mother to night;
verses.4:6: My people have become like one who has no knowledge. Because you rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from serving as priest to Me; and you forgot the law of your God, and I also will forget your children.
verses.4:7: According to their multitude, so they sinned against Me; I will turn their glory into dishonor.
verses.4:8: They will eat the sins of My people, and in their injustices they will take their souls.
verses.4:9: And it will be, just as the people, so also the priest; and I will avenge his ways upon him, and I will repay his plans to him.
verses.4:10: And they will eat and will by no means be filled; they prostituted themselves and will by no means prosper, because they abandoned the Lord to keep
verses.4:11: prostitution. And the heart of My people received wine and strong drink.
verses.4:12: They inquired by omens, and by his staffs they reported to him; by a spirit of prostitution they were led astray, and they prostituted themselves away from their God.
verses.4:13: On the tops of the mountains they sacrificed, and on the hills they made offerings under an oak and a white poplar and a shading tree, because shelter is good. Therefore your daughters will prostitute themselves, and your daughters-in-law will commit adultery.
verses.4:14: And I will by no means call your daughters to account when they prostitute themselves, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery; for they themselves mingled with the prostitutes, and they made offerings with the initiated ones, and the people who understand were intertwined with a prostitute.
verses.4:15: But you, Israel, do not be ignorant; and Judah, do not go into Gilgal, and do not go up to the house of On, and do not swear by the living Lord.
verses.4:16: Because like a frenzied heifer, Israel has become frenzied; now the Lord will pasture them like a lamb in a wide place.
verses.4:17: A partner of idols, Ephraim has set stumbling blocks for himself,
verses.4:18: he chose Canaanites. Prostituting themselves, they utterly prostituted themselves; they loved dishonor from her arrogance.
verses.4:19: You are a whirling wind in her wings, and they will be put to shame because of their altars.
verses.5:1: Hear these things, priests, and pay attention, house of Israel, and house of the king, listen closely, because the judgment is against you; for you have become a snare to the watchtower, and like a net spread out over Tabor,
verses.5:2: which those who hunt prey have fixed firmly. But I am your discipliner.
verses.5:3: I have known Ephraim, and Israel is not absent from Me. For now Ephraim has prostituted himself; Israel has been defiled.
verses.5:4: They have not given their plans to return to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is in them, and they have not known the Lord.
verses.5:5: And the arrogance of Israel will be humbled to his face, and Israel and Ephraim will grow weak in their injustices, and Judah also will grow weak with them.
verses.5:6: With sheep and calves they will go to seek out the Lord, and they will by no means find Him, because He has turned away from them.
verses.5:7: For they abandoned the Lord, because foreign children were born to them; now the blight will devour them and their allotments.
verses.5:8: Sound a trumpet on the hills, resound on the heights, proclaim in the house of On. Benjamin was astounded;
verses.5:9: Ephraim has come to ruin in the days of rebuke. Among the tribes of Israel I have shown trustworthy things.
verses.5:10: The rulers of Judah have become like those who move boundaries; upon them I will pour out My fury like water.
verses.5:11: Ephraim oppressed his adversary; he trampled judgment, because he began to go after worthless things.
verses.5:12: And I am like turmoil to Ephraim, and like a goad to the house of Judah.
verses.5:13: And Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his pain; and Ephraim went to the Assyrians and sent envoys to King Jarim. And he was not able to heal you, and pain will by no means cease from you.
verses.5:14: Because I am like a panther to Ephraim, and like a lion to the house of Judah; and I will seize and go away, and I will carry off, and there will be no one who rescues.
verses.5:15: I will go and return to My place, until they are brought to ruin and seek My face. In their affliction they will rise early to Me, saying:
verses.6:1: "Let us go and return to the Lord our God, for He Himself has seized and will heal us; He will strike and will bandage us;
verses.6:2: He will make us well after two days; on the third day we will also rise up,
verses.6:3: and we will live before Him, and we will know. We will pursue knowing the Lord; like a ready dawn we will find Him, and He will come to us like early and late rain to the earth."
verses.6:4: What shall I do to you, Ephraim? What shall I do to you, Judah? For your mercy is like a morning cloud and like early dew that goes away.
verses.6:5: Therefore I cut down your prophets; I killed them by the word of My mouth, and My judgment will go forth as light.
verses.6:6: Because I desire mercy rather than sacrifice, and knowledge of God rather than whole burnt offerings.
verses.6:7: But they are like a man who transgresses a covenant; there Gilead despised Me, a city
verses.6:9: and your strength is that of a bandit; priests hid the way, they murdered Shechem, because they committed lawlessness
verses.6:10: in the house of Israel. I saw horrifying things there, the prostitution of Ephraim; Israel and Judah were defiled. Begin to harvest for yourself
verses.6:11: when I bring back the captivity of My people,
verses.7:1: When I heal Israel, then the iniquity of Ephraim and the wickedness of Samaria will be revealed, because they practiced falsehoods; and a thief will come in to him, a robber plundering on his road,
verses.7:2: so that they may sing together like those singing in their heart. I have remembered all their wicked deeds; now their designs have surrounded them; they have come before My face.
verses.7:3: With their wicked deeds they gladdened kings, and with their lies, rulers.
verses.7:4: All of them are committing adultery, like an oven burning for baking with scorching heat from the flame, from the kneading of dough until it is leavened.
verses.7:5: The days of your kings—the rulers began to become enraged from wine; he stretched out his hand with pestilent men.
verses.7:6: Because their hearts were kindled like an oven, while they were crashing down, all night Ephraim was filled with sleep; morning came; it was kindled like a brightness of fire.
verses.7:7: All of them grew hot like an oven, and they devoured their judges; all their kings fell; there was no one among them calling upon Me.
verses.7:8: Ephraim was mingling himself among his peoples; Ephraim became a hearth cake not turned over.
verses.7:9: Foreigners devoured his strength, yet he did not know; and gray hairs sprouted on him, and he did not know.
verses.7:10: And the arrogance of Israel will be humbled to his face, yet they did not return to the Lord their God, nor did they seek Him out in all these things.
verses.7:11: And Ephraim was like a senseless dove, having no heart; he was calling upon Egypt, and they went to the Assyrians.
verses.7:12: As they go, I will cast My net over them; like the birds of the sky I will bring them down; I will discipline them at the report of their affliction.
verses.7:13: Woe to them, because they leaped away from Me; they are wretched, because they acted impiously against Me. I redeemed them, yet they spoke falsehoods against Me.
verses.7:14: And their hearts did not cry out to Me, rather they were wailing on their beds; for grain and wine they were cutting themselves.
verses.7:15: They were disciplined by Me, and I strengthened their arms, yet against Me they devised evil.
verses.7:16: They turned away to nothing; they became like a stretched bow. Their rulers will fall by the sword because of the lack of discipline of their tongue; this is their mockery in the land of Egypt.
verses.8:1: Into their bosom like earth, like an eagle against the house of the Lord, because they transgressed My covenant and against My law.
verses.8:2: To Me they will cry out, "God, we have known You."
verses.8:3: Because Israel rejected good things, they pursued an enemy.
verses.8:4: They reigned for themselves, and not through Me; they ruled, and did not inform Me; their silver and their gold they made into idols for themselves, so that they might be utterly destroyed.
verses.8:5: Rid yourself of your calf, Samaria! My wrath has been provoked against them; how long will they be unable to be cleansed
verses.8:6: in Israel? And a craftsman made it, and it is not a god; because your calf was a deceiver, Samaria.
verses.8:7: For they sowed wind-blighted crops, and their ruin will receive them—a sheaf having no strength to produce flour; and even if it does produce, foreigners will devour them.
verses.8:8: Israel has been swallowed up; now he has become among the nations like a useless vessel.
verses.8:9: For they themselves went up to the Assyrians; Ephraim flourished by himself, they loved gifts;
verses.8:10: therefore they will be handed over among the nations. Now I will take them in, and they will cease for a little while from anointing a king and rulers.
verses.8:11: Because Ephraim multiplied altars, beloved altars became sins for him.
verses.8:12: I will write down a multitude for him, and My statutes were counted as foreign things—the beloved altars.
verses.8:13: For if they offer a sacrifice and eat meat, the Lord will not accept them; now He will remember their iniquities and punish their sins. They returned to Egypt, and among the Assyrians they will eat unclean things.
verses.8:14: And Israel forgot the One who made him, and they built shrines; and Judah multiplied walled cities; and I will send out fire into his cities, and it will devour their foundations.
verses.9:1: Do not rejoice, Israel, nor be glad like the peoples; because you played the prostitute away from your God, you loved gifts on every threshing floor of grain.
verses.9:2: Threshing floor and winepress did not know them, and the wine deceived them.
verses.9:3: They did not dwell in the land of the Lord; Ephraim dwelt in Egypt, and among the Assyrians they will eat unclean things.
verses.9:4: They did not pour out wine to the Lord, and they were not pleasing to Him; their sacrifices are like bread of mourning to them; all who eat them will be defiled, because their loaves for their souls will not enter into the house of the Lord.
verses.9:5: What will you do in the days of a festal assembly and on the day of a feast of the Lord?
verses.9:6: Therefore, look, they are going away from the distress of Egypt, and Memphis will receive them, and Machmas will bury them; their silver—destruction will inherit it; thorns in the tents.
verses.9:7: The days of punishment have come, the days of your recompense have come, and Israel will be afflicted like the prophet who is out of his mind, the spirit-bearing man; because of the multitude of your iniquities, your madness has been multiplied.
verses.9:8: Ephraim is a watchman with God; a prophet is a crooked snare on all his ways; they planted madness in the house of God.
verses.9:9: They became corrupt as in the days of the hill; He will remember their iniquities; He will punish their sins.
verses.9:10: Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel, and like an early watchman in a fig tree I saw their fathers; they themselves went in to Baal-peor, and they were alienated into shame, and the detested ones became like the beloved ones.
verses.9:11: Ephraim flew away like a bird—their glories from births and birth pains and conceptions.
verses.9:12: For even if they bring up their children, they will be made childless from among mankind; for woe also is to them—My flesh is from them.
verses.9:13: Ephraim, just as they presented their children for prey, so also Ephraim is to bring out his children for stabbing.
verses.9:14: Give to them, Lord—what will You give them? A childless womb and dry breasts.
verses.9:15: All their wicked deeds are in Gilgal, for there I hated them because of the wickedness of their practices; out of My house I will drive them; I will not continue to love them; all their rulers are disobedient.
verses.9:16: Ephraim has suffered pain; he has dried up in his roots; he will no longer bear fruit; for even if they give birth, I will kill the cherished ones of their womb.
verses.9:17: God will reject them, because they did not listen to Him, and they will be wanderers among the nations.
verses.10:1: Israel is a vine rich in branches; its fruit is plentiful. According to the abundance of its fruits, he multiplied altars; according to the good things of his land, he built pillars.
verses.10:2: They divided their hearts; now they will be destroyed. He Himself will demolish their altars; their pillars will come to ruin.
verses.10:3: For now they will say, "We have no king, because we did not fear the Lord. And what will the king do for us,
verses.10:4: speaking words, false pretexts?" He will make a covenant; judgment will spring up like wild grass on the untilled ground of a field.
verses.10:5: Those who dwell in Samaria will sojourn beside the calf of the house of On, because its people mourned over it; and just as they provoked it, they will rejoice over its glory, because it was deported from it.
verses.10:6: And having bound it, they carried it off to the Assyrians as gifts for King Jarim; Ephraim will receive a gift, and Israel will be put to shame in his counsel.
verses.10:7: Samaria cast off her king like a twig on the surface of water.
verses.10:8: And the shrines of On, the sins of Israel, will be removed; thorns and thistles will come up over their altars; and they will say to the mountains, "Cover us," and to the hills, "Fall on us."
verses.10:9: From the time of the hills, Israel sinned; there they stood. War will by no means overtake them on the hill against the children of injustice
verses.10:10: to discipline them. And peoples will be gathered against them when they are disciplined for their two injustices.
verses.10:11: Ephraim is a heifer trained to love strife, but I will come upon the finest part of her neck; I will mount Ephraim, I will pass over Judah in silence, Jacob will grow strong for him.
verses.10:12: Sow for yourselves for righteousness, harvest for the fruit of life, light for yourselves a light of knowledge; seek out the Lord until crops of righteousness come to us.
verses.10:13: Why did you pass over ungodliness in silence, and harvest its injustices, and eat false fruit? Because you hoped in your sins, in the abundance of your strength,
verses.10:14: destruction will indeed rise up among your people, and all your fortified places will be gone. Just as the ruler Shalman from the house of Jeroboam, in days of war they dashed mother to the ground upon children,
verses.10:15: so I will do to you, house of Israel, because of the injustice of your evils.
verses.11:1: At dawn they were cast off; the king of Israel was cast off. For Israel was a young child, and I loved him, and out of Egypt I summoned his children.
verses.11:2: Just as I summoned them, so they departed from My presence; they kept sacrificing to the Baals and burning incense to the carved images.
verses.11:3: And I bound the feet of Ephraim; I took him up onto My arm; they did not know that I have healed them.
verses.11:4: In the destruction of people, I stretched them out with the bonds of My love, and I will be to them like a man slapping on his cheeks; and I will look toward him, I will prevail over him.
verses.11:5: Ephraim lived in Egypt, and Assyria itself was his king, because he was unwilling to return.
verses.11:6: And he grew weak by the sword in his cities, and he ceased in his hands; and they will eat from their counsels.
verses.11:7: And his people hang suspended from his dwelling; and God will be enraged at his precious things, and will by no means exalt him.
verses.11:8: What shall I do with you, Ephraim? Shall I shield you, Israel? What shall I do with you? I will make you like Admah and like Zeboiim. My heart turned around at the same time; My regret was thrown into turmoil.
verses.11:9: I will by no means act according to the anger of My wrath; I will by no means abandon Ephraim to be blotted out, because I am God and not a man, the Holy One in you, and I will not enter into a city.
verses.11:10: After the Lord I will walk; like a lion He will bellow, because He Himself will roar, and children of the waters will be astounded.
verses.11:11: They will fly out like a bird out of Egypt, and like a dove out of the land of the Assyrians; and I will restore them to their homes, says the Lord.
verses.12:1: Ephraim surrounded Me with falsehood, and the house of Israel and Judah with ungodliness. Now God has known them, and they will be called a holy people of God.
verses.12:2: But Ephraim is an evil spirit; he pursued scorching heat all day long. He multiplied empty and futile things, and he made a covenant with the Assyrians, and he traded oil to Egypt.
verses.12:3: And the Lord has a judgment against Judah, to punish Jacob according to his ways, and according to his practices He will repay him.
verses.12:4: In the womb he seized his brother by the heel, and in his toils he proved strong with God,
verses.12:5: and he proved strong with an angel and prevailed. They wept and pleaded with Me; in the house of On they found Me, and there it was spoken to them.
verses.12:6: Now the Lord God Almighty will be His memorial.
verses.12:7: And you will return in your God; guard mercy and judgment, and draw near to your God continually.
verses.12:8: Canaan: in his hand is a balance of injustice; he loved to oppress.
verses.12:9: And Ephraim said, "Yet I have become rich; I have found relief for myself." None of his labors will be found for him because of the injustices in which he sinned.
verses.12:10: But I, the Lord your God, brought you up out of the land of Egypt; I will again make you live in tents, as in the days of a festival.
verses.12:11: And I will speak to prophets, and I multiplied visions, and by the hands of prophets I was likened.
verses.12:12: If it is not Gilead, then the rulers sacrificing in Gilead were false, and their altars are like tortoises on the untilled ground of a field.
verses.12:13: And Jacob withdrew to the plain of Syria, and Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept guard.
verses.12:14: And by a prophet the Lord brought Israel up out of the land of Egypt, and by a prophet he was guarded.
verses.12:15: Ephraim aroused wrath and provoked anger; and his blood will be poured out upon him, and the Lord will pay back his reproach to him.
verses.13:1: According to the word of Ephraim, he himself received ordinances in Israel, and he established them for Baal and died.
verses.13:2: And they continued to sin, and they made for themselves a cast image from their silver according to the likeness of idols, works of craftsmen completed for them; they themselves say, "Sacrifice human beings, for calves have come to an end."
verses.13:3: Therefore they will be like a morning cloud and like early dew passing away, like chaff blown away from a threshing floor, and like vapor from tears.
verses.13:4: Yet I am the Lord your God, establishing heaven and creating earth, whose hands created all the host of heaven, and I did not show them to you so that you would walk after them; and I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and you will know no god besides Me, and there is no one who saves apart from Me.
verses.13:5: I shepherded you in the wilderness, in an uninhabited land,
verses.13:6: according to their pastures; and they were filled to the full, and their hearts were lifted up; because of this they forgot Me.
verses.13:7: And I will be to them like a panther and like a leopard along the way of the Assyrians;
verses.13:8: I will meet them like a bear in distress, and I will tear open the enclosure of their heart, and lion cubs of the forest will devour them there; wild beasts of the field will tear them apart.
verses.13:9: In your destruction, Israel, who will help?
verses.13:10: Where is this king of yours? And let him deliver you in all your cities; let him judge you, the one about whom you said, "Give me a king and a ruler."
verses.13:11: And I gave you a king in My anger, and I held back in My wrath.
verses.13:12: A conspiracy of Ephraim's injustice; his sin is hidden.
verses.13:13: Labor pains like those of a woman giving birth will come upon him. This is your wise son, because he will by no means endure in the crushing of children.
verses.13:14: Out of the hand of Hades I will rescue and out of death I will redeem them. Where is your penalty, Death? Where is your sting, Hades? Comfort is hidden from My eyes,
verses.13:15: because this one will divide between brothers. The Lord will bring a scorching wind out of the wilderness upon him, and He will dry up his veins; He will lay waste his springs; He Himself will completely dry up his land and all his desirable vessels.
verses.14:1: Samaria will be wiped out, because she opposed her God; they themselves will fall by the sword, and their nursing infants will be dashed to the ground, and their pregnant women will be torn open.
verses.14:2: Return, Israel, to the Lord your God, because you have grown weak in your injustices.
verses.14:3: Take words with you and return to the Lord your God; speak to Him so that you may not receive injustice and may receive good things, and we will repay the fruit of our lips.
verses.14:4: Assyria will by no means save us; we will not mount a horse; we will no longer say, "Our gods," to the works of our hands; the one who is in You will show mercy to an orphan.
verses.14:5: I will heal their dwellings, I will love them openly, because he has turned My anger away from him.
verses.14:6: I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like a lily, and he will put forth his roots like Lebanon.
verses.14:7: His branches will go forth, and he will be like an olive tree laden with fruit, and his fragrance will be like that of Lebanon.
verses.14:8: They will return and sit under his shelter; they will live and be intoxicated with grain; and a vine will blossom forth as his memorial, like wine of Lebanon.
verses.14:9: As for Ephraim, what does he still have to do with idols? I humbled him, and I will strengthen him; I am like a dense juniper; from Me your fruit has been found.
verses.14:10: Who is wise and will understand these things? Or who is discerning and will recognize them? For the ways of the Lord are straight, and the righteous will walk in them, but the ungodly will grow weak in them.

notes.1:4: The Greek text reads "on the house of Judah" (ἐπὶ τὸν οἶκον Ἰούδα), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "on the house of Jehu."
notes.1:6: The Greek renders the closing clause as "but rather I will surely oppose them" (ἀλλ᾽ ἢ ἀντιτασσόμενος ἀντιτάξομαι αὐτοῖς), differing from the debated Hebrew clause often translated "that I should forgive them at all."
notes.1:7: The Greek text reads simply "the sons" (τοὺς δὲ υἱοὺς) without specifying "of Judah," whereas the Hebrew MT and some Greek witnesses specify the house or sons of Judah.
notes.2:1: The Greek begins with the past-tense imperfect ἦν ("was") before shifting to future verbs, and adds "they also" (καὶ αὐτοὶ) in the closing promise. Verses 2:1-2:25 in the Septuagint correspond to 1:10-2:23 in the Hebrew MT.
notes.2:4: The Greek reads first-person "I will remove ... from My presence" (ἐξαρῶ ... ἐκ προσώπου μου) and continues in 2:5 with a positive purpose clause "so that I may strip her naked" (ὅπως ἂν ἐκδύσω), whereas the Hebrew MT urges her to remove prostitution from her own face "lest" God strip her.
notes.2:14: The Greek reads "a testimony" (εἰς μαρτύριον) where the Hebrew MT has "a forest," and expands the devourers to include "the birds of the sky and the creeping things of the earth," matching 2:20.
notes.2:17: The Greek contains several distinct readings compared to the Hebrew MT: "her possessions" (MT "her vineyards"), "to open up her understanding" (MT "for a door of hope"), "she will be humbled" (MT "she will answer/sing"), and "her infancy" (MT "her youth").
notes.2:18: The Greek reads plural Βααλείμ ('Baals,' transliterated 'Baalim') rather than Hebrew singular 'my Baal,' matching 'the Baals' in 2:15, 2:19, and 11:2.
notes.2:25: Here the Greek shifts from "mercy" (ἐλεέω in 1:6-2:6) to "love" (ἀγαπήσω τὴν Οὐκ ἠγαπημένην, "I will love Not Loved," echoed in Rom 9:25), and expands the closing reply to the full confession "You are the Lord my God."
notes.3:1: The Greek reads "who loves evil things" (ἀγαπῶσαν πονηρὰ) where the Hebrew MT reads "loved by a companion/lover," and uses "God" (ὁ θεός) where the MT uses the divine name.
notes.3:2: The Greek uses the verb "hired" (ἐμισθωσάμην) and reads "a jar of wine" (νέβελ οἴνου, transliterating Hebrew nebel, a wine-jar or skin-bottle) where the Hebrew MT reads "a lethech [half-homer] of barley."
notes.3:4: Where the Hebrew MT lists sacred pillar, ephod, and teraphim, the Greek reads "altar" (θυσιαστηρίου), "priesthood" (ἱερατίας), and "manifestations" (δήλων, the standard Septuagint term for the priestly Urim).
notes.4:5: Here and in verse 6, the Septuagint uses the verb homoioo ("liken" / "become like"), reflecting a reading of the Hebrew root as "resemble" rather than "destroy" or "cut off."
notes.4:10: In the Septuagint, "to keep" at the end of verse 10 governs "prostitution" at the start of verse 11, and the remainder of verse 11 makes "the heart of My people" the subject that received wine and strong drink.
notes.4:14: The Greek tetelesmenon ("the initiated ones") refers to cultic initiates (where the Hebrew has cult prostitutes), and the final clause reads positively "the people who understand" without the negative found in the Hebrew text.
notes.4:15: The Septuagint renders the place name as "the house of On" (oikon On, echoing the Egyptian city On) rather than Hebrew "Beth-aven" (so also in 5:8).
notes.4:18: The Septuagint reads "he chose Canaanites" (and in verse 17 "set stumbling blocks for himself"), diverging sharply from the Hebrew text ("leave him alone; their drink is gone").
notes.5:1: The Septuagint translates Hebrew "Mizpah" as the common noun "the watchtower" (skopia) and continues in verse 2 with a relative clause describing the hunting net fixed down by hunters of prey.
notes.5:7: The Septuagint reads "the blight" (erysibe, crop mildew or blight) where the Hebrew text reads "the new moon" (or "a month").
notes.5:8: The Septuagint renders Hebrew "Gibeah" and "Ramah" as common nouns ("the hills" and "the heights"), repeats "the house of On" (cf. 4:15), and reads "Benjamin was astounded" rather than "Behind you, Benjamin!"
notes.5:12: Instead of the Hebrew metaphors of a moth and rottenness, the Septuagint reads "turmoil" (tarache) and "a goad" (kentron).
notes.5:13: "King Jarim" preserves the Septuagint proper name Iareim (corresponding to Hebrew yareb, often rendered "Jareb" or "the great king"), and the Greek explicitly states that Ephraim sent "envoys."
notes.6:2: The Septuagint reads "He will make us well" (hygiasei) and intransitive "we will also rise up" (anastesometha), and places "and we will live before Him" at the opening of verse 3 rather than the end of verse 2.
notes.6:3: The Septuagint reads "like a ready dawn we will find Him" (heuresomen auton), taking the Hebrew form from the verb "to find" rather than "His going forth."
notes.6:5: In the Septuagint, "your prophets" is the direct object of "I cut down" (apetherisa, literally "mowed down"), and the final clause reads "My judgment will go forth as light."
notes.6:10: The Septuagint verse divisions differ from the Hebrew in verses 7-11: verse 7 begins the clause about Gilead (continued in verse 8 with "troubling water"), and verse 10 joins "and Judah" to "Israel was defiled" before beginning the command "Begin to harvest for yourself," which continues into verse 11.
notes.7:2: The Greek reads "so that they may sing together like those singing in their heart," diverging from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "they do not consider in their heart."
notes.7:4: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew "heated by a baker" as "burning for baking with scorching heat," omitting any explicit mention of a baker ceasing to stir the fire.
notes.7:6: The Greek verb rendered "crashing down" (katarasso) is difficult here, and the Septuagint reads "Ephraim was filled with sleep" where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "their baker sleeps."
notes.7:16: The Greek reads "a stretched bow" (entetamenon) and "lack of discipline" (apaideusian), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "a treacherous/slack bow" and "insolence/rage."
notes.8:1: The Septuagint opens with "Into their bosom like earth" (reflecting a different reading of the Hebrew consonants behind MT's "To your lips a trumpet") and leaves the final phrase "and against My law" elliptical without a second verb.
notes.8:3: The Greek makes "enemy" the direct object of a plural verb ("they pursued an enemy"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text makes the enemy the subject ("an enemy shall pursue him").
notes.8:6: The Greek participle "a deceiver" (planon, lit. "leading astray") diverges from the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "broken in pieces / splinters."
notes.8:7: The Septuagint renders the imagery as "wind-blighted crops" and "their ruin" rather than the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "wind" and "whirlwind."
notes.8:12: The Greek divides the clauses differently from the Hebrew Masoretic Text, reading "a multitude" separately from "My statutes" and closing the verse with "the beloved altars" (corresponding to the opening words of MT 8:13).
notes.9:6: The Septuagint connects "Egypt" to "distress" and preserves the distinctive proper name Machmas (cf. Michmash), translating a Hebrew word that the Masoretic Text reads as "precious things" ("their precious things of silver").
notes.9:9: The Greek translates the place name Gibeah literally as a common noun, "the hill" (tou bounou).
notes.9:10: The Septuagint reads "an early watchman in a fig tree" (skopon) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "the firstfruit on the fig tree," and renders the closing clause "the detested ones became like the beloved ones."
notes.9:12: The Greek concludes with "My flesh is from them," reading the Hebrew consonants as "My flesh" rather than the Masoretic Text's "when I depart from them."
notes.9:13: The Septuagint reads "for prey" (eis theran) where the Hebrew Masoretic Text refers to "Tyre," and "for stabbing" (eis apokentesin) for MT's "to the slayer."
notes.10:5: The Greek reads "the house of On" (corresponding to Hebrew "Beth-aven"), translates the verb as "sojourn beside" rather than "fear," and reads "just as they provoked it, they will rejoice" where the Hebrew refers to its idol-priests.
notes.10:6: The Greek names "King Jarim" (Hebrew "Jareb" or "the great king") and reads literally "in a gift Ephraim will receive," diverging from the Hebrew "Ephraim will receive shame."
notes.10:9: The Greek renders the place name "Gibeah" as a common noun ("the hills" / "the hill") and states the war clause as an emphatic negation continuing into the infinitive at the start of 10:10.
notes.10:11: The Greek reads "strife" (neikos, sometimes understood by itacism as nikos, "victory") instead of Hebrew "threshing," and translates "pass over in silence" here and in 10:13 by taking the Hebrew verb hrsh as "be silent" rather than "plow."
notes.10:14: The Greek reads "the ruler Shalman from the house of Jeroboam," where the Hebrew refers to Shalman's devastation of Beth-arbel.
notes.11:1: Following Septuagint versification, the opening sentence about the king of Israel corresponds to the end of 10:15 in Hebrew; the verse also reads "his children" (plural) where the Hebrew has "my son."
notes.11:3: The Greek verb synepodisa literally means "I bound the feet of," differing from the Hebrew "I taught to walk."
notes.11:4: The Greek diverges sharply from the Hebrew here, reading "in the destruction of people," "like a man slapping on his cheeks," and "I will prevail over him" instead of "with cords of a man," "like those who lift a yoke," and "I fed them."
notes.11:9: The Greek reads "abandon Ephraim to be blotted out" and translates the final phrase "into a city," taking the Hebrew consonants as "in a city" rather than "in wrath."
notes.11:10: The Greek shifts to the first person singular ("I will walk") and renders the Hebrew "from the west/sea" as "children of the waters."
notes.12:1: The Greek joins "and Judah" to the first clause and reads "Now God has known them, and they will be called a holy people of God," diverging from the Hebrew (numbered 11:12 in Hebrew and most English Bibles).
notes.12:5: The Greek shifts to plural verbs ("they wept," "pleaded with Me," "found Me"), uses a passive ("it was spoken to them"), and reads "the house of On" where the Hebrew has "Bethel."
notes.12:6: The Greek pronoun autou may refer either to God ("His memorial," designating His covenant title) or to Jacob ("his memorial").
notes.12:11: The Greek uses a future tense ("I will speak") and a passive verb ("I was likened," meaning represented through prophetic similitudes), where the Hebrew has past and active forms.
notes.12:12: The Greek names Gilead twice (instead of Gilead and Gilgal), reads "rulers" instead of Hebrew "bulls," and renders the altar simile as "tortoises" (chelonai) rather than Hebrew "stone heaps."
notes.13:2: The Greek reads "Sacrifice human beings, for calves have come to an end," diverging sharply from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("those who sacrifice men kiss calves").
notes.13:3: The Greek literally reads "vapor from tears" (apo dakryon), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text has "smoke from a lattice" or "chimney."
notes.13:4: The Greek includes an extended creation clause concerning the heavens and their host and supplies the verb "I brought you up," neither of which appears in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.13:13: Unlike the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("an unwise son" at the opening of the womb), the Greek reads "your wise son" (often understood ironically) and "in the crushing of children."
notes.13:14: The Greek asks "Where is your penalty, Death?" (dike), differing from both the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("your plagues") and Paul's quotation in 1 Corinthians 15:55 ("your victory").
notes.14:3: The Greek renders the clause after "speak to Him" as a second-person plural purpose clause ("so that you may not receive injustice") before shifting to first-person plural ("we will repay the fruit of our lips," contrasting with the Hebrew Masoretic Text's "bulls of our lips").
notes.14:4: The Greek closes with an active construction ("the one who is in You will show mercy to an orphan"), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text uses a passive verb ("in You the orphan finds mercy").
notes.14:5: Following the Greek text, this verse reads "dwellings" (MT "apostasy"), "openly" (homologos; MT "freely"), and a transitive third-person verb ("he has turned My anger away from him," where MT makes "My anger" the subject).
notes.14:8: The Greek omits a comparative particle before "vine," linking "vine" directly to "his memorial"; "be intoxicated with grain" translates the Greek verb methyskomai literally in its sense of abundant satiety.
notes.14:9: The Greek reads "I humbled him, and I will strengthen him" and specifies a "juniper" (arkeuthos), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "I answer and look after him" and "cypress."
